title: Casper and the Harvest
premise: Bram Delacroix, a hospice nurse who has spent a decade rationalizing the backwards-counting voices of the dying, returns to their family's decaying farmhouse in Harrow Bend when an excavation crew unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside. As the harvest moon rises, the door opens, and Bram learns the counting was never death—it was an invitation, renewed each generation by a Delacroix, and this year no one renewed it. Trapped in the house with the crew and the thing that has worn their family's faces for two centuries, Bram must choose between completing the ritual that would make them the next vessel or burning the inheritance down. At dawn, Bram walks out alone, having fed the house its own name instead of blood—but the counting has started again, and now it's coming from inside them.
about_author: Quentin Galloway is the pen name of a former night-shift caregiver who spent six years in rural palliative care before turning to fiction. They write horror about inheritance, small towns, and the things families agree not to discuss.

chapters.title: The Backwards Count
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In a hospice outside Harrow Bend, Bram hears their final patient count down from ten in a voice not her own, then go silent with a smile. Ten years of rationalizations begin to crack. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm; Bram realizes the counting always ends at one, never zero.

chapters.title: Letters from a House That Hates You
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A lawyer's letter summons Bram to the Delacroix farmhouse, inherited after an aunt's death—the aunt who died counting. Flashbacks reveal Bram fled at nineteen after hearing the cellar 'breathing.' Emotional beat: reluctant homecoming; belonging as a wound reopened.

chapters.title: What the Excavation Found
chapters.summary: Crew foreman Denny Okafor's POV. The crew digging a septic line strikes a stone door beneath the yard—hinges on the inside, no handle outside, warm to the touch. Old-timer crew member refuses to work past sundown. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness; the land itself seems complicit.

chapters.title: Sealed from Within
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram arrives to find the crew camped in the yard, refusing to leave until morning. In the attic they find generations of ledgers: every Delacroix signed a page each harvest, names written backwards. The last entry is blank, dated tomorrow. Emotional beat: identity as obligation; Bram sees their own handwriting already on the page.

chapters.title: One of Us Was Never Invited
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, shifting between Bram and Denny. Night falls early. The power dies, phones show calls placed from inside the house—by Bram's dead aunt. Something knocks politely at every door in sequence. Emotional beat: isolation tightening; the group fractures between skeptics and believers.

chapters.title: The Faces It Kept
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the root cellar beside the sealed door, Bram finds photographs of every Delacroix across two centuries—each aged identically, each wearing Bram's face by the final picture. The thing below doesn't haunt the family; it rehearses them. Emotional beat: horror of recognition; inheritance as erasure.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. The crew tries to flee; the driveway loops back to the house no matter which way they drive. One by one, crew members begin counting backwards in their sleep. Denny wakes to find his own mouth moving. Emotional beat: loss of bodily autonomy; panic curdling into fatalism.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The sealed door opens inward on its own. Below, something wearing Aunt Verity's face explains the covenant gently: sign the ledger, become the vessel, spare everyone—or refuse and let it take them all. It offers what Bram always wanted: to finally belong somewhere. Emotional beat: seduction; the monster as family.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, climax. Bram signs the ledger—but writes the house's own true name, scraped from the foundation stones, instead of theirs. The thing must honor an invitation addressed to itself. The house begins consuming its occupant as the survivors run; Bram stays to hold the ledger open like a wound. Emotional beat: sacrifice through cleverness; reclaiming identity by giving the inheritance away.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, resolution. Dawn. Bram walks out of the smoking ruin, alive but changed, and takes Denny's silence as payment for survival. Weeks later, back at the hospice, a new patient grips Bram's wrist and counts—from zero upward. Emotional beat: ambiguous survival; belonging achieved at the cost of becoming the invitation.
